In the current PR, you created functions just to name what a piece of code was doing. This is not really the point of functions—they're aimed at reducing complexity when the code they're hosting is supposed to be used at several places.

The code on the screenshot is way more straightforward. Later on, we'll feel confident removing a piece of code because it's inlined. Creating functions brings a mental overhead that creates friction when times comes to refactor/delete code (e.g., "this function had a name, we probably knew what we meant with this, let's not remove it").

From the outside, we (the team, the contributors, and yourself in a few days) understand the inlined code way better because it reads from top to bottom easily—with the functions, we jump from one statement to another, loosing track of what gets executed and when it gets executed.

I'd recommend reading "[Goodbye, Clean Code](https://overreacted.io/goodbye-clean-code/)".
